newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes up on export talk, commercials.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes up on export talk, commercials.

text.p: CBOT wheat ended higher on export talk, commercial buying and short covering, traders said.
"In wheat it was short covering, March was oversold," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Nearby March was higher on commercial buying, traders said. Cargill Inc bought 3.0 million bushels of March, traders said and Continental Grain bought one million March.
Export sources Wednesday said Iraq on February 11 would seek 50,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat and Egypt was in the market for 165,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian wheat.
But traders were skeptical the U.S. would land any of the business and most cited short covering as the reason for the rally in wheat futures Wednesday.
July gains were limited by forecasts for possible beneficial snow and rain this week in the U.S. Plains hard red winter wheat region.
"Personally, I think it's too early to worry about but they're saying snow in the Plains is calming down concerns over dry weather," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Wheat closed one to 3-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 3-3/4 at $3.61-1/2.
March Tuesday dropped to a new contract low of $3.56-1/2 and the market now is very oversold, traders said.
Technicians cited first support in the March at $3.55-1/2 and second support at $3.50-1/2. First resistance is at $3.60-1/2 and second resistance is at $3.65-1/2.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for March closed near 32 percent. The market generally views an RSI of 30 or less as indicative of an oversold market.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 13,500 contracts, below the 14,932 traded Tuesday.
In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 350 March $3.70 calls at 2-1/4 cents and Tenco Inc sold 200 May $3.70 calls at 6-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,500 contracts, below the 6,559 traded Tuesday.
